'''Fore''' or '''Foré''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|f|ɔːr|eɪ}} {{respell|FOR|ay}}<ref>Laurie Bauer, 2007, ''The Linguistics Student’s Handbook'', Edinburgh</ref>) is a [[Kainantu-Goroka languages|Kainantu-Goroka language]] spoken in the [[Goroka District]] of [[Eastern Highlands Province]], [[Papua New Guinea]].

All the dental consonants can vary to alveolar, except /t̪/ which is always dental. /p/, /t̪/, and /k/ are pronounced as /b~β/, /ɾ~l/, and /g~ɣ/ between vowels, and /p~ɸ/, /t̪~t/, /k~x/ word initially/.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fatkhiyati |first=Nurrahma |date=2023-02-19 |title=Morphological process found in Fore language in Papua New Guinea |url=https://doi.org/10.21009/lililacs.031.02 |journal=Lililacs Journal|volume=3 |issue=1 |pages=15–23 |doi=10.21009/lililacs.031.02 |issn=2807-8845|doi-access=free }}</ref> Velar consonants are labialized after rounded vowels. /j/ is often pronounced as a fricative /ʝ/.

It also has four diphthongs: ae, ao, ai, and au.

Fore has a [[Pitch-accent language|pitch accent]] system. Each syllable is either accented or unaccented. Multiple accented syllables can occur in the same word, but they cannot be adjacent to each other.
